full_judgment:
9. The learned Counsel Mr AJ Mohammad Ali with Ms Bilkis Jahan appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the petitioner was dismissed from his service on a false and baseless allegation that he attempted to outrage the modesty of a girl Sabina Yeasmin, student of Class VIII of the school. The learned Counsel next submits that according to the Non-Government Secondary School Teacher Regulation (Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education of Rajshahi) under Rule 12 although the power to impose penalty upon a teacher under Regulation II shall vest in the authority competent to make appointment but the penalty of dismissal or removal from service shall not be imposed unless the proposal for such penalty is examined by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee and approved by the Board under Rule 12. He further submits that since the impugned order of dismissal being not approved by the Board after examination by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee the order of dismissal became void and without jurisdiction. Finally, the learned Counsel submits that the impugned order of dismissal of the petitioner from his service is passed without any lawful authority and the same was passed in violation of the rule of natural justice. Hence the decision of the Appeal and Arbitration Committee should prevail upon the impugned order of dismissal, as such, order of dismissal passed by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and the petitioner should be reinstated in the service with all service benefits. 

 12. The learned Counsel for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 raised another point that the writ petition is also bad for non joinder of necessary party viz, Ambari Bahumukhi Uccha Biddalaya and its Managing Committee whose presence is indispensable for giving effect to any order that may be passed by this court. Finally, he submits that since the writ petition is not at all maintainable and there is no substance in the writ petition the Rule should be discharged. 

 "A recognised non-government secondary school does neither become a statutory body nor a 'local authority' within the meaning of the General Clauses Act. That being the position in law, the appellant does not become disqualified for being a Chairman of the Union Parishad under section 7(2)(e) of the Ordinance of 1983 by reason of being a full-time teacher of the Sammilani Girls" High School." 

 The very fact that it is a Non-government Girl's High School is sufficient to exclude any such writ petition because it is not a body constituted or established by the government. It has not been possible on the part of the learned Advocate for the petitioner to refer any law under which the said school has been constituted or established. It is however, true that the school like any other non-government secondary school is regulated and managed in accordance with the provision of the Ordinance of 1961 and the various regulations made thereunder. The governments have control over those schools in a very large manner nevertheless, it is clear from what has been discussed above and thereby a recognised non-government secondary school does neither become a statutory body nor a local authority within the meaning of the General Clauses Act.
